Presenter is Kavya Mehta, not the claude-liam/Nik Bear Brown persona: no IN-FOR-BEAR framing, no @NikBearBrown branding anywhere in this reel. ClaudeTitleOutro was deliberately NOT used for the outro because its '@NikBearBrown' handle is hardcoded in the component source (runtime/remotion/src/scenes/ClaudeTitleOutro.tsx:19) with no prop override. ClaudeVerdictArtifact (no hardcoded branding) is used as the closing card instead, same pattern as kavya-brutalist-week1-progress and kavya-brutalist-week2-progress.
metadata.note: ai-explainer recap of this session's own real, verifiable work — third in the sequel series after kavya-brutalist-week1-progress and kavya-brutalist-week2-progress. Every claim is real: reel three (claude-liam-opentelemetry-ai-agents) built end to end — landscape render, compile, vertical derivation, portrait render, compile — with zero new bugs or defects found, the first fully clean build in the series (week 1 had 6 infra bugs, week 2 had 1 component bug). The honest caveat stated on screen is also real: this build reused only components already exercised by reels 1 and 2, so a zero-bug build does not by itself prove the pipeline is bug-free for genuinely new component shapes. No code shown anywhere. Built to satisfy docs/FELLOWS-SUBMISSION.md's required-content rules: the required intro line opens B00's narration verbatim, AI-narration is disclosed in the same beat, and this reel renders native 16:9 (3840x2160) and 9:16 (2160x3840).

beats.narration_text: Hi, I am Kavya, and this video is about my third week with the Brutalist video pipeline. This narration is AI-generated with Kokoro text-to-speech, reading a script I wrote and reviewed. Six bugs in week one. One bug in week two. This week: zero. Is the pipeline actually stable now — or did this build just get lucky?

beats.narration_text: Here's the idea: week three doesn't mean the pipeline is bug-free. It means this one build hit no new edge case. That's a smaller claim — and a truer one.

beats.narration_text: Four things to track. A third reel got built — OpenTelemetry for AI agents, same shape as the last two. Zero new bugs surfaced, the first clean build in the series. Every claim still got checked against a real exported frame, not a preview. And the trend across three reels: six fixes, then one, then zero. A trend, not a guarantee.

beats.narration_text: Here's the actual count, week by week. Week one: six bugs, all in shared infrastructure — encoding, subprocess calls, missing dependencies. Week two: one bug, in a component week one had already touched. Week three: zero. The same build, run the same way, hit nothing new.

beats.narration_text: Don't over-read a zero. This build reused every component the last two reels already exercised — no new layout, no new props shape. A zero here means the known paths are solid. It says nothing about the next genuinely new component.

beats.narration_text: Recap: three reels in, six bugs then one then zero — a declining trend, not a guarantee. This week reused only proven components, so no new code paths actually got exercised. The verification habit held regardless — every claim checked against a real frame. The honest read: a stable pipeline isn't one that never needs checking. It's one that keeps getting checked anyway.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. If your last few builds went clean, don't just relax. Ask Claude exactly this: my last three builds had zero new bugs, before I assume it's solid, help me find one thing about the next build that's genuinely different from the last three, so I know what's actually still unverified.
